notes:
This is a handwritten mathematical leaf numbered 4 at bottom left, without a date or separate title. It begins with the lower-case continuation encore une fois and ends with the unfinished Alors on a. Neither endpoint is completed editorially. Displays (11), (12), and (13), the circled section number 4, both square-bracket levels in the upper comment, all source abbreviations, and the revised material are retained. No other page was read for this return.

The word germe in the opening line has a separate underline beneath its latter letters, distinct from the g descender. The source reads seulement des phi_xi and ss groupe, without replacing ss by H’s s- form. M0641 resolves to mod. The bracketed hypothesis says s’envoie injectivement. The first verb has an initial e-loop, compressed n/v sequence, late dotted i and final e; it lacks the g descender that C’s s’immerge would require. The large descending stroke alongside it belongs to the j of injectivement. The last phrase before (11) is connaît ce germe, not son germe.

In (11), the limit index is Gamma-prime subset Gamma, with ouvert on the following line. There is no separate dotted underline beneath ouvert; H’s note appears to confuse the word’s low connected strokes with such a line. Since H already mentions ouvert, no whole-word omission is alleged there. Both target capitals are the cursive E form, not Sigma. Inside the Hom parentheses, the old small cluster immediately to the right of E is blackened/cancelled and a replacement X is written below E. The possible barred X from C is retained only under uncertainty; the dense cancellation prevents a secure recovery of its original strokes. H does acknowledge a cancelled argument, but its note places that argument after Hom(...), rather than inside the parentheses as an older subscript. The quotient slash is heavily retraced; Int and the subsequent pi_1(X), E_X arguments are nevertheless readable.

The next comment literally begins [et = l’image, using two horizontal strokes for the abbreviation même. The sign is retained rather than expanded. H omits the written abélien after H^1. M0642 resolves to the three short ellipsis marks after convenable. The two closing square brackets are distinct and both are preserved.

The 4 introducing the next section has a round enclosing contour, not parentheses. The enclosure around D=sum D_i has an open underside, an outward left baseline foot, a rounded roof and a curled right foot. It is drawn rather than replaced by a closed rectangle. The raised effectif has its own leader running underneath it and bending down after diviseur. That leader accounts for the parenthesis-like stroke H places after un diviseur; there is no parenthesis pair around those two words.

The component parenthesis reads I l’ens de ses comp. irréd. Here the final sentence punctuation in this English note is not source punctuation: in the TeX the abbreviation irréd is immediately followed by the source closing parenthesis, with no terminal dot. Likewise l’ens has no period. The separated accent over e and looped d are visible; the small gap before d is treated as ordinary letter spacing, not a separate word. M0643 is recorded as other because the exact joined form differs from the strings in C’s mark, but a space-only grouping decision is not counted as a separate substantive C collation error. H’s added period is recorded. The source writes mult. and gén., which remain abbreviated.

The addition (i.e. lisse) is raised between régulier and en les. Its pale opening curve is close to the i but sufficiently separate to retain the opening parenthesis, at medium confidence; its closing parenthesis and long descending leader are clear. The en les words are legible, resolving H’s local doubt without a certainty-only row. The cancelled label following Soit is X_I: the lower I has separate upper and lower horizontal bars. This resolves C’s unnumbered deletion doubt without changing H’s reading. The new (13) uses an explicit prime on its left-hand X and a single minus stroke before supp D.

After (13), le sous-groupe and the later On le notera are singular as written. In the group subscript, there are only two punctuation clusters: an elongated upper mark after the first X and a lower comma. The leading reading X-prime, X uses precisely those two marks. The alternative X;X remains possible if they form one semicolon. No extra middle dot is supplied to create X-prime;X. This is an ink decision, not a normalization to an expected group notation.

The small word H calls ouvert under that group index is encore, inserted above the notera/(par region. Its under-running curve descends to the gap before the separate opening parenthesis of (par abus de notation); the parenthesis is not miscounted as a second leader. The refinement --|ou plus précisément G_X-prime(I). is a separate raised addition after the baseline G_X-prime and comma, before Alors on a. Its long leader is preserved and is not read as an opening parenthesis before a D. Its prefix remains uncertain between a broken dash and compressed ou. The common letters précisém are readable; the last low strokes are compressed and crowded by the descender of par above. Full ent remains the preferred ending, with abbreviated t retained as an alternative in place, rather than silently expanding an uncertain abbreviation. The detached prime before (I) and the period after it are visible. Alors on a remains an unfinished clause without an added final stop.

check_events.statement: The germ construction by restriction to common finite-index subgroups is compatible with quotienting homomorphisms by conjugation from the fixed kernel group.
check_events.outcome: For finite-index subgroups H1,H2 of Gamma, the diagonal coset map Gamma/(H1 intersection H2) into Gamma/H1 times Gamma/H2 is injective, so the intersection has finite index and provides a common restriction domain. If k belongs to the fixed conjugating subgroup and f is a homomorphism, then (k f k^{-1}) restricted to H equals k(f restricted to H)k^{-1} pointwise. Thus restriction carries conjugacy classes consistently, and equality after restriction can be checked on a common finite-index subgroup. This verifies the elementary compatibility used in the written germ/Int expression, not the arithmetic injectivity assertion for xi.

check_events.statement: For a formal reduced divisor D=sum_i D_i with distinct prime components and coefficient 1, an automorphism preserving the set of prime components preserves D, and conversely; this is equivalent to preservation of its support and open complement.
check_events.place: Formula (12), sans comp. mult., definition (13), and following stabilizer sentence
check_events.outcome: An automorphism sends each prime D_i to a prime and sends the formal sum to sum_i g(D_i). Equality of the formal divisors is equivalent to a permutation of the distinct components because every coefficient is 1. An automorphism preserving their union permutes its irreducible components, giving the converse from support preservation. Taking complements then gives g(X minus supp D)=X minus supp D. This argument is expressly about the formal reduced component sum; it does not identify arbitrary scheme structures on the same support or settle the punctuation of the group subscript.
